archive.note: the file size matches the layout arithmetic computed before any download

decode.exact: weights are scales[row, col // group] * (code - 1); float32 adds no error
decode.sanity: packed qweight bytes span 0..242 with mean 119.9, exactly the base-3 five-digit distribution

reader_bug_found.symptom: the first decode reported the right parameter count but produced unusable weights
reader_bug_found.cause: safetensors data_offsets are relative to the start of the data section, and the reader seeked to the absolute file position, discarding the section start
reader_bug_found.evidence: LayerNorm weights read as 1.8e37 with the absolute seek; 0.103 mean and 0.032 std with the corrected seek; scales were negative before and are all positive after
reader_bug_found.lesson: a parameter-count match validates shapes, not values. Byte-level sanity checks on decoded tensors are not optional.

teacher_graph_correspondence.method: compare dense LayerNorm weights, which no quantization touches
teacher_graph_correspondence.conclusion: the validated teacher encoder graph is the same architecture and model family, so redux weights can be written into it. The two weight sets are close but not bit-equal, which matches a quantization-aware repack.
teacher_graph_correspondence.shape_mapping: teacher exposes 217 anonymous MatMul constants shaped [4096,1024]x49, [1024,4096]x48, [1024,1024]x120, matching redux's linears and pointwise convolutions
teacher_graph_correspondence.risk: the MatMul constants are anonymous, so the mapping is by graph order and must be verified numerically per tensor rather than assumed

not_done: the substitution has not been performed; no oracle gate has been run for redux
the decoder and prediction-network weights live outside the encoder graph and still need an export path
